This research addresses these interconnected challenges by investigating how fine-tuning techniques can be applied to develop an effective, cost-efficient AI learning support system specifically designed for Vietnamese flipped classroom education.

4.2.1 Dataset Composition

The training dataset consists of historical student-AI conversational records provided by the research supervisor, supplemented where necessary by structured prompting of existing LLMs to address topic gaps in the original corpus. The combined raw dataset was not in a state suitable for direct fine-tuning use and was therefore processed through the eight-step quality pipeline described in Section 3.2 (and detailed in Chapter 4, Section 4.2.2) prior to use in training.

Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is the most successful PEFT approach. It freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable low-rank matrices into each layer, reducing trainable parameters by up to 10,000x while maintaining quality. QLoRA extends LoRA by quantizing frozen weights to 4-bit precision, enabling fine-tuning of very large models on consumer GPUs.

LoRA represents state-of-the-art parameter-efficient fine-tuning. It operates on the insight that weight updates during fine-tuning have low intrinsic rank. QLoRA extends this by storing frozen weights in 4-bit precision, enabling fine-tuning of large models (e.g., 7B–13B parameters) on consumer-grade GPUs such as the NVIDIA T4 (16GB VRAM). The Hugging Face Transformers library, PEFT library, and Unsloth framework together provide the primary technical stack for this research.

EXPERIMENTAL AND RESULTS

The most pronounced improvements were observed in pedagogical dimensions. The proportion of responses classified as guided inquiry (scaffolded, questioning, or step-by-step) increased from an average of 12% in baseline models to 68% in fine-tuned models (high-quality data configuration). Direct answer provision decreased from 71% to 19% on average. Vietnamese language quality scores improved by 34% on average, with particular gains in subject-specific terminology accuracy.

The results support a theoretical framing of fine-tuning as behavioral alignment—shaping how the model interacts rather than merely what it knows. The behavioral shift from answer-giving to guided inquiry demonstrates that SFT alone, with carefully curated pedagogical data, can achieve meaningful alignment. The empirical evidence also contributes to an emerging theoretical understanding of data quality in fine-tuning: pedagogical quality dimensions are distinct from and more impactful than generic quality dimensions.

The consistent pattern of improvement across all three base models—in both technical and pedagogical dimensions—suggests that LoRA fine-tuning reliably adapts general-purpose LLMs to educational interaction patterns when training data explicitly models desired pedagogical behaviors. The fine-tuned model demonstrated a substantial shift from direct-answer behavior toward guided inquiry responses, as assessed by the AI Judge evaluation framework. Prior to fine-tuning, the base model consistently provided direct answers to student queries. After fine-tuning, the model exhibited guided scaffolding behavior across evaluated test samples.

- Base Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B

Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is the most successful PEFT approach. It freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable low-rank matrices into each layer, reducing trainable parameters by up to 10,000x while maintaining quality. QLoRA extends LoRA by quantizing frozen weights to 4-bit precision, enabling fine-tuning of very large models on consumer GPUs.

LoRA represents state-of-the-art parameter-efficient fine-tuning. It operates on the insight that weight updates during fine-tuning have low intrinsic rank. QLoRA extends this by storing frozen weights in 4-bit precision, enabling fine-tuning of large models (e.g., 7B–13B parameters) on consumer-grade GPUs such as the NVIDIA T4 (16GB VRAM). The Hugging Face Transformers library, PEFT library, and Unsloth framework together provide the primary technical stack for this research.

This study encompasses the following technical boundaries: subject coverage spans taught in Vietnamese secondary and high school education; the primary language of instruction and interaction is Vietnamese; base models include LLaMA 3, Mistral, and Qwen; fine-tuning methodology focuses on LoRA and related PEFT techniques; the dataset comprises approximately 746 curated student-AI conversation samples; and the web-based platform includes administrative and student-facing functional modules.

The results confirm the core technical feasibility of the proposed approach: parameter-efficient fine-tuning on modest Vietnamese educational datasets can produce meaningfully improved AI tutoring behavior, deployable within academic resource constraints. The data quality findings have direct practical implications for institutions seeking to develop similar systems, suggesting that investment in expert data curation yields greater returns than investment in data quantity or compute scale.

A qualitative comparison of models trained on curated versus unfiltered data consistently demonstrated that higher data quality produced meaningfully better pedagogical alignment, confirming the data-centric hypothesis central to this study. Quantitative comparison of quality-controlled versus unfiltered configurations is presented in Section 4.3, provides robust empirical support for prioritizing data curation over data quantity in educational fine-tuning pipelines.
